title: Exploring How Agent Voice Accents Shape Human-AI Collaboration in K-12 Group Learning
title_zh: 探索 Agent 语音口音如何影响 K-12 小组学习中的人机协作
abstract_en: Collaboration is widely recognized as a cornerstone of 21st-century education, yet teachers still encounter persistent challenges in fostering productive peer interaction. LLM conversational peer agents introduce new possibilities for mediating in-person group work, raising questions about how persona design, particularly their voice characteristics, shapes learners' perceptions, trust, and interactional dynamics. While prior work has examined agent accent effects in one-to-one settings, little is known about how these effects manifest in groups. We conducted a between-subjects mixed-methods study with 33 teachers examining how a GenAI voice agent with different accents (British, Indian, and African American) influenced collaboration and agent perception. Across surveys, group interaction analyses, and artifacts, we find that accent shaped participants' mental models and the roles the agent assumed in group interaction. The British-accented agent was largely treated as a tool and engaged in detached, utility-based ways, whereas Indian- and African American-accented agents were more readily anthropomorphized and integrated as peers. These role expectations influenced trust, engagement, and reliance over time. This work advances understanding of how GenAI's sociolinguistic design features shape group dynamics in CSCL, with implications for designing culturally inclusive AI partners in group learning.
abstract_zh: 协作被广泛视为 21 世纪教育的核心能力，但教师在促进高质量同伴互动方面仍面临持续挑战。基于 LLM 的对话式同伴 Agent 为线下小组学习提供了新的调解方式，也引出了关于 persona design（人格化设计），尤其是语音特征如何影响学习者感知、信任与互动动态的问题。既有研究多关注一对一场景中的 Agent 口音效应，而其在群体协作中的表现仍缺乏了解。本文开展了一项包含 33 名教师的组间 mixed-methods study，考察带有不同口音的 GenAI 语音 Agent——British、Indian 和 African American——如何影响协作过程与 Agent 感知。通过问卷、小组互动分析和学习产物，研究发现口音会塑造参与者对 Agent 的 mental models 以及 Agent 在群体互动中被赋予的角色。British-accented Agent 多被视为工具，并以较疏离、功用导向的方式被使用；而 Indian- 和 African American-accented Agent 更容易被拟人化，并被整合为同伴。这些角色预期进一步影响了随时间变化的信任、参与度和依赖程度。该研究推进了对 GenAI 社会语言学设计特征如何塑造 CSCL 群体动态的理解，并对设计文化包容的 AI 学习伙伴具有启示意义。
key_points_zh: 研究聚焦 K-12 group learning 中 GenAI voice agent 的口音设计，比较 British、Indian 和 African American 三种口音对人机协作的影响。
采用组间 mixed-methods study，包含 33 名教师，并结合问卷、小组互动分析与学习产物进行评估。
British-accented agent 更常被参与者视为工具，互动方式偏疏离和实用导向。
Indian- 与 African American-accented agents 更容易被拟人化，并被纳入小组互动中作为类似同伴的角色。
Agent 口音通过影响学习者的 mental models 和角色预期，进一步改变信任、参与度与依赖关系，对文化包容的 CSCL AI partner 设计具有重要意义。

llm_assessment.comment: An interesting HCI study on voice-agent accent effects in group learning, but it contributes little to realtime agent systems, tool use, or reusable technical infrastructure.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 这是一项关于语音智能体口音影响小组学习的有趣HCI研究，但对实时智能体系统、工具使用或可复用技术基础设施贡献有限。
